newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS BOUNCE BACK, BLANKING GIANTS 27-0.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS BOUNCE BACK, BLANKING GIANTS 27-0.

text.p: Troy Aikman completed a pair of first-quarter touchdown passes and the Cowboys held the Giants to just 96 yards of offence, bouncing back from a dreadful loss in their opener to blank New York 27-0 Sunday.

Aikman completed 19-of-27 passes for 228 yards, including touchdowns to Deion Sanders, Kevin Williams and Emmitt Smith. Smith, who shook off injuries to his neck and shoulder suffered in Monday night's 22-6 loss in Chicago, started and carried 25 times for 94 yards and a touchdown.
Pulled early in the fourth quarter, he saw his streak of six 100-yard rushing games against New York come to an end.
"We executed a lot better than last week," said Aikman. "This was a big game for us."
Dave Brown was under pressure all game for the Giants. He completed 10-of-19 passes for 55 yards and an interception.
"I thought we played excellently in every facet of the game," said Barry Switzer, coach of the Super Bowl champion Cowboys.
In San Francisco, defensive tackle Bryant Young had three sacks as the 49ers had seven sacks, two safeties and held the St Louis Rams to just 104 yards of offence in a 34-0 shutout.
San Francisco (2-0) had three rushing touchdowns for the second straight week and has yet to have a passing touchdown this season.
In Seattle, John Elway passed for two touchdowns and ran for another and Jason Elam kicked three field goals to lead the Denver Broncos to a 30-20 victory over the Seahawks.
Terrell Davis, who rushed for more than 1,000 yards as a rookie last season, gained 111 yards on 28 carries for Denver.
The Broncos improved to 2-0 for the first time since 1993. Seattle slipped to 0-2.
In Washington, Terry Allen's 28-yard touchdown run with 4:49 left in the third quarter snapped a tie and the Redskins survived a last-minute drive to post a 10-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

With the score tied, 3-3, the Bears drove to the Redskins' 20-yard line in the third quarter before receiver Michael Timpson caught a short pass -- but and fumbled the ball to cornerback Darrell Green. Washington then went 61 yards on three plays to take the lead for good.

In Kansas City, cornerback James Hasty returned a fumble by quarterback Billy Joe Hobert 80 yards for a touchdown and the Chiefs continued their domination of AFC West rival Oakland with a 19-3 victory over the Raiders.
Chiefs All-Pro linebacker Derrick Thomas sacked Hobert to force the fumble. He also had a safety in the fourth quarter.
The Chiefs have won seven straight and 13 of the last 14 meetings from the Raiders, and have scored a defensive touchdown in four straight games against Oakland.
The Raiders again played without injured starting quarterback Jeff Hostetler.

In Buffalo, Jim Kelly and Quinn Early hooked up on a tie-breaking 63-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter and the Bills stuffed the New England Patriots on a game-ending goal line stand to hold on for a 17-10 victory.
In Atlanta, Brad Johnson threw a pair of TD passes and led the Minnesota Vikings to their second straight win without the injured Warren Moon, a 23-17 triumph over the Falcons.
Minnesota improved to 2-0 for the first time since 1987.
Atlanta dropped its first two games for the third time in six years.

In Detroit, Barry Sanders rushed for 125 yards and a touchdown and Corey Raymond returned an interception for a score as the Lions overcame a slow start for a 21-6 victory over the punchless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Sanders amassed 109 yards on just 10 carries in the first half. His 288 rushing yards lead the NFL.
In New Orleans, John Kasay kicked five field goals for the second straight game, including a 27-yarder with 2:09 remaining to lift the Carolina Panthers to a 22-20 victory over the Saints.
The Panthers (2-0) did not win until the sixth week of their expansion season last year.

At New York, Jim Harbaugh carved up the Jets' secondary (15-for-20, 242 yards), passed for one touchdown and ran for another as the Indianapolis Colts improved to 2-0 for the first time in 19 years with a 21-7 victory.
The game was delayed by lightning for 32 minutes in the third quarter. It is believed to be the first regular-season contest in NFL history to be halted due to weather.

In Pittsburgh, Mike Tomczak completed 18-of-25 passes for 198 yards and two touchdowns in his first start of the season and Rod Woodson returned an interception 43 yards for a TD to lead the Steelers to a 31-17 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
After a loss at Jacksonville with Jim Miller as quarterback, Steelers coach Bill Cowher switched to Tomczak.
In San Diego, Leonard Russell scored on a pair of one-yard plunges and the Chargers completed a two-game season-starting home sweep with a 27-14 triumph over the Cincinnati Bengals.
In Jacksonville, Chris Chandler threw for three touchdowns and rookie Eddie George had his first 100-yard rushing game as the Houston Oilers held off the Jaguars 34-27.

At Arizona, rookie Karim Abdul-Jabbar scored on a pair of three-yard runs in the first half and Dan Marino threw a pair of touchdown passes as the Miami Dolphins built a big lead and rolled to a 38-10 demolition of the Cardinals.
The Dolphins have won their first two games under new coach Jimmy Johnson and dropped Arizona and its new head man Vince Tobin to 0-2.
